hook_text: Push this plunger and that one comes out. Fill it with air and it feels like a sponge. Fill it with water and it feels like a rod.
clip_script: Two syringes, same size, joined by a tube. Push the master in, the slave comes out, same distance, same force, a push sent round a corner. That is fluid power: car brakes, excavator arms, rescue cutters. Now the trick. Air inside, pneumatic: push and it squashes first, spongy, then moves, then springs back. Water inside, hydraulic: push and it moves instantly, solid, no spring. Gas compresses, liquid does not. Test it fairly: dry first, then filled under water so no bubbles hide inside, same pushes, same masses, write it down. One pea-sized bubble turns your hydraulic system into a pneumatic one.
visual_style: Whiteboard two syringes and a tube; arrows along the tube; an air version compressing with a spring icon; a water version moving as a rigid bar; a bubble crossed out.
pacing: The system, the transfer, air versus water, the fair test and the bubble warning.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and feel the difference with two syringes and a straw.
